prerequisites: It is recommended not to take this subject until a comprehensive view of the technical disciplines taught in the degree has been achieved.

learning_outcomes.text: Ability to write, sign and develop projects in the field of industrial engineering that aim at the construction, reform, repair, conservation, demolition, manufacturing, installation, assembly or exploitation of: structures, mechanical equipment, energy installations, industrial installations and plants and manufacturing processes.
Ability to manage the activities that are the object of the engineering projects described in the previous section.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity and critical reasoning.
Ability to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills and abilities in the field of Engineering, both orally and in writing, and to all types of audiences.
Knowledge for carrying out measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert reports, studies, reports, work plans and other similar tasks.
Ability to handle specifications, regulations and mandatory standards.
Ability to analyze and assess the social and environmental impact of technical solutions.
Ability to apply quality principles and methods.
Ability to organize and plan within a company, and other institutions and organizations.
Ability to work in a multilingual and multidisciplinary environment.
Knowledge, understanding and ability to apply the necessary legislation in the exercise of the Industrial Technical Engineer profession.
Ability to prevent occupational hazards and protect the health and safety of workers and users.
Honesty, responsibility, ethical commitment and spirit of solidarity.
Ability to work in a team.
Knowledge and skills to organize and manage projects. Know the organizational structure and functions of a project office.
Understand the requirements and legal and ethical implications of professional engineering practice, particularly in project development.
Know the characteristics of projects, their life cycle and the technical, economic, safety, environmental, legal, social and ethical conditions to be considered in them.

Define the scope of a project and plan the deadlines and costs of all tasks necessary to carry it out, and monitor the progress and supervision of the work to be carried out in a project, keeping the initial planning in mind.
Clearly explain and adequately justify the solutions adopted in a project, preparing the associated documents that allow its contracting and execution.
Know the structure and functions of a technical office, as well as develop and improve a work method.

teaching_methods: Classroom practices (problem solving and case studies)
Computer lab practices (planning, budgeting, graphic and document management tools)
assessment_rules: To pass in the ordinary call, it is mandatory to obtain a minimum of 5 out of 10 points in each of the three parts (EV-1, EV-2, EV-3). If these minimums are met, the final grade is calculated as 0.4 * EV-1 + 0.35 * EV-2 + 0.25 * EV-3. Otherwise, the grade will be the minimum between the calculated grade and 4.0. For EV-2, the grade is the average of two individual works, provided each work is >4.0; otherwise, the minimum of the average and 4.0 is taken. For EV-3, the grade is 0.5 * (exercises in class) + 0.5 * (laboratory practices exam). In the extraordinary call, grades >5 in any EV can be kept; if retaken, the new grade applies. For differentiated evaluation, attendance to practices is not mandatory, and EV-3 is calculated as 0.25 * (exercises submitted) + 0.75 * (laboratory practices exam) for the ordinary call, and only the lab exam for the extraordinary call.
